thread:
jamal: incident-bot alerted: node gpu-pool-12 root /scratch at 98% -> multiple serve-runtime pods terminated due to OOM and container restart loops. seeing modelcache crashes. paging SRE.
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: disk_utilization_high on gpu-pool-12 (root: 98%). threshold=90%. Auto-notify: #incidents, oncall.
oncall-bot: Paging SRE oncall: @maya (primary) @jamal (reporter)
maya: I'm on it. quick ask — do we have a customer-facing route impacted? any 5xx spikes? :eyes:
jamal: yes, some 503s from the hosted API for requests routed to gpu-pool-12. latency up for a subset of gen requests. customers A,B reported errors via support.
ellie: grabbing logs from pod serve-runtime-7a9c. short log tail:
```
[2026-06-05T14:02:12Z] modelcache: loading shard 3 -> mmap failed: no space left on device
[2026-06-05T14:02:15Z] runtime: Alloc failed, CUDA error: out of memory
[2026-06-05T14:02:16Z] serve: container exited: code=137
```
jamal: modelcache tried to write checkpoints and fill then OOM. multiple pods got killed by OOM killer. node also reporting journal writeback stalls.
akshay: can we cordon node and move live workloads? I can kick a drain and reschedule but need capacity in region.
maya: coordinate now. ops-lead @ellie you'll need to run emergency cleanup on /scratch to free model cache + logs. priority: remove old debug dumps and rotated logs older than 2d.
ellie: running quick check:
```
$ ssh gpu-pool-12
# du -sh /scratch/* | sort -h
120G model-dumps-2025-*/
85G training-checkpoints/
42G serve-logs-old/
```
ellie: I'm safe-deleting serve-logs-old/* and moving model-dumps-2025 -> temporary archival bucket. starting deletes now. will keep 3 most recent.
maya: @akshay start draining non-critical pods off gpu-pool-12. set pod disruption budget ignore for canaries.
akshay: running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-pool-12
kubectl drain gpu-pool-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
jamal: warning — drain is slow, some pods in Completed state with large local volumes. consider increasing eviction grace to speed cleanup.
ellie: freed ~140GB by deleting old logs and rotated dumps. /scratch at 63% now. modelcache processes starting to come up but some containers still crash immediately with CUDA OOM.
maya: good progress. check node dmesg for kernel OOM vs container-level OOM. if it's container-level, maybe quantized model variant fallback is needed.
ellie: dmesg snapshot shows repeated GPU driver timeouts and cuda context resets. Likely a cascade: disk fill -> partial model load -> mem blow -> driver reset -> crash.
akshay: I spun up two replacement nodes in the same AZ and tied new pods to them. traffic shifting via routing policy should reduce load on the impacted node.
ops-lead: updating status on incident command: impact = partial (subset of gen traffic 5xx), mitigation = node cordoned + cleanup, new capacity provisioned. no confirmed data exfiltration.
jamal: support: notified customers A,B with ETA ~15m. adding temporary reroute to fallback model variant with smaller ram footprint while we stabilize.
maya: roll change: apply rollout policy to route 40% to fallback-small for affected routes:
```
api update-route --route gen --fallback-model small-quantized --weight 40
```
ellie: modelcache pods stabilized after cleanup but one serve-runtime still exits with code 137 and logs show:
```
2026-06-05T14:25:01Z runtime: failed to alloc 2.3G for KV cache
2026-06-05T14:25:01Z runtime: CUDA error: out of memory
```
maya: we should temporarily disable large KV prefetch on that model for the node group. Akshay can you patch config:
```
modelcache.config.kv_prefetch=false
```
akshay: patch applied to rollout group. restarting affected pods.
oncall-bot: handoff reminder — current oncall @maya running mitigation. ETA for stability 20m. if persists escalate to infra lead.
jamal: logs look cleaner and 5xx rate dropped to baseline for the past 8m. keeping one node cordoned until we confirm no latent crashes.
ops-lead: will open an internal postmortem ticket. immediate action items: 1) add disk liveness probe for /scratch usage, 2) limit local debug dump retention to 5GB per node, 3) automated archival to S3 for large dumps.
ellie: filing quick followup: I'll push a temporary cron to rotate logs hourly and a cleanup job for >48h files.
maya: thanks everyone. if anything pops, re-alert on this thread. handing off to next oncall @akshay in 30m for follow-up checks. :white_check_mark:
